acts.desc: It's hard to give things up. Host Ira Glass tells the story of Walter, a three-year-old boy who had to give up his pacifier, and then, wanting comfort, asked all the adults around him to tell the stories of when they gave up their pacifiers.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Nubar Alexanian was forced to give up one thing—and then gave up another thing by choice. This story was put together by Nubar and his daughter Abby, with help from Jay Allison, for Transom.org, with funding from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.
acts.title: Do You Hear What I Hear?

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Ira with former baseball player Bobby Morris, on leaving baseball.
acts.title: Yerrrrr Out!

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
Every week, Chelsea Merz has lunch with a homeless man named Matthew, in the same restaurant. Matthew's been on the street for seven years, but once or twice a year, he housesits for a friend. She talked to him after he was housesitting for 16 days, on the day he went back out on the street. This story is part of a larger project Chelsea is putting together, with help from Jay Allison, the Cape and Island NPR stations, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.
Since we first broadcast this story, Matthew has gotten off the street. He now gives talks around the country about his experience.
acts.title: The Call Of The Great Indoors

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Sometimes it's hard to figure out if you're doing something of your own choice or because someone wants you to do it. Actor Matt Malloy reads "Guilt," a short story by Judith Budnitz.
acts.title: Tin Man
